source.title: Implicit Self-Regularization in Deep Neural Networks: Evidence from Random Matrix Theory and Implications for Learning
source.authors: Charles H. Martin; Michael W. Mahoney

record.tranche_reason: The study varies training batch size on MiniAlexNet trained on CIFAR-10 and reports training accuracy, which bears on V1's training-error outcome. It does not report the accuracy values in text.
record.gate_note: The authors' general statement that deep learning drives training error to zero is background, not a result of this study. Other reported spectral measurements do not measure the claim versions. The batch-size training-accuracy values are shown only in Figure 29.
record.test_reason: MiniAlexNet is trained from random initialization with momentum SGD on CIFAR-10 and evaluated using training classification accuracy, matching V1's method and measure. Its small architecture and early stopping are relevant conditions, but the supplied text does not reveal absolute training accuracies.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the batch-size result: training accuracy is roughly flat through batch size 100 and then decreases, while smaller batches improve test accuracy and strengthen spectral signatures of self-regularization. More broadly, the authors propose a random-matrix taxonomy of implicit self-regularization and interpret these batch-size results as explaining the generalization gap.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes weight-matrix spectra and batch-size effects rather than comparing the cited gradient-training recipes for reaching near-zero classification error. It reports training accuracy for MiniAlexNet on CIFAR10.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size: the text says training accuracy is roughly flat until b ≈ 100, then begins to decrease; test accuracy also varies with batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors' retrained LeNet5 reaches 100.00% training accuracy after 20 epochs with AdaDelta on MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A LeNet5 variant trained with AdaDelta can attain zero training classification error on MNIST.

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller batches produce stronger spectral signatures of implicit self-regularization and better test accuracy in MiniAlexNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size affects learned weight spectra and generalization in MiniAlexNet.

record.problems: Training-accuracy values relevant to V1 appear only in a figure, so the supplied text does not establish whether they are near zero error. The text reports no uncertainty for those values.
record.rows_left_out: None. Other results concern spectral metrics, test accuracy, or cited prior work, and do not measure the outcomes named in the claim versions.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, sufficiently large CNNs, model-size comparisons, Adam, and controlled comparisons of stopping rules.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-minimum frequencies, and extra student neurons.
Training-error comparisons across depths, identity shortcuts, and the special initialization exceptions.
Initialization comparisons measuring learning speed or trainable depth; using Glorot initialization alone does not test these effects.
Learning rates relative to an initial stability threshold, loss recovery, curvature trajectories, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Training-speed and learning-rate-tolerance comparisons with and without batch normalization, and Fixup.

missing.what: Baseline MiniAlexNet training-accuracy trajectories for an ensemble of 10 runs at batch size 16 without explicit regularization. These outcomes are omitted despite measuring V1's training-error construct; numerical values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

MiniAlexNet training-accuracy trajectories with and without L2 weight regularization and Dropout. These comparisons are relevant to V1's regularized-recipe clause, contrary to rows_left_out's coverage statement; their absolute values and differences are unavailable in the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict is justified from unreadable absolute accuracies: a plateau or relative decrease alone cannot establish either near-zero error or substantial residual error. Early stopping is an actual experimental condition, not an untested feature. The LeNet5 result falls outside V1's specified datasets and optimizers. Weight-matrix spectra are not Hessian curvature and do not test V5; the statement that removing batch normalization leaves results unchanged does not establish V6's speed or stability outcomes.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, comparisons across model sizes, early stopping, optimizers, and whether the reported CIFAR-10 runs reach zero or near-zero training error.
